body.text: tatra vidyāyā vedyarūpatve veditṛsvarūpatve vā doṣamāha

children.translated_text: 'If the nature of the known' —
thus. Since neither of those has the capacity to remove <s>avidyā</s>, even <s>vidyā</s> having their nature would absurdly lack the capacity to remove <s>avidyā</s> — such is the meaning.
'Of yours' —
after this,
'in the view'
is to be supplied. He states the fault if it has the nature of consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>):
'Consciousness itself' —
thus.
Since consciousness is eternally established and all-pervading, <s>avidyā</s>, being of the nature of its absence, would simply be unestablished — such is the purport. (104)

body.translated_text: There, he states the fault if <s>vidyā</s> has the nature of the known (<s>vedya</s>) or the nature of the knower (<s>veditṛ</s>):

body.text: kiñceyaṃ tadviruddhā vā, na tasyāḥ kvāpi sambhavaḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, if this [<s>avidyā</s>] is contradictory to that [consciousness], then there is no possibility for it anywhere,
Since the entire world is pervaded by <s>vidyā</s> (consciousness), which is without a second. (Verse 105)

children.translated_text: 'Moreover this' —

children.text:
iti /
divākarakaravyāpte deśe divākare vā tadvirodhino 'ndhatamasasyeva vibhvyā saṃvidā vyāpte sarvatra saṃvidi vā nāvidyāyāḥ samāveśasambhava ityarthaḥ /
vidyābhinnāvidyetyapi durvacamevādvaitavādibhiriti sūcyate
children.translated_text: thus. Just as darkness, which is opposed to the sun, has no place in a region pervaded by the sun's rays, or in the sun itself, so <s>avidyā</s> cannot find entry anywhere — in everything pervaded by consciousness or in consciousness itself. Such is the meaning. It is also indicated that [the claim of] <s>avidyā</s> being non-different from <s>vidyā</s> is equally difficult for the Advaitins to maintain —
'Without a second' —
by this. (105)

body.translated_text: He states the objection if <s>vidyā</s> is consciousness and <s>avidyā</s> is contradictory to it:
If <s>avidyā</s> is accepted as the absence of consciousness, or as something contradictory to it, or even [as something else],
Then you should abandon from afar the thesis of the non-duality of consciousness (<s>saṃvidadvaita</s>). (Verse 106)

children.translated_text: (Thus the exposition of the impossibility of the indescribable nature of <s>avidyā</s>.)
He states the objection applicable to all three alternatives:
'Absence' —

children.text:
iti /
saṃvidabhāvādirūpānādiravidyāsti cet , saṃvidevaikāstīti bhavadabhimatamadvaitaṃ na sidhyediti bhāvaḥ /
nanu saṃvinmātraṃ paramārthasaditi paramārthaikyamevāsmākamabhimatam /
children.translated_text: thus. If there exists a beginningless <s>avidyā</s> of the nature of the absence of consciousness, or of some other nature, then the non-duality accepted by you — that consciousness alone exists — would not be established. Such is the purport. Objection: Our accepted position is precisely the ultimate oneness — that mere consciousness alone is ultimately real.

children.text: avidyāyā aparamārthatvena tadanāditve 'pi nāsmadabhimatādvaitoparodha iti cedatra bramaḥ-anāditvenopagamyamānāyā avidyāyāḥ kalpakadoṣāntarāyogenāpāramārthyāyogaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since <s>avidyā</s> is not ultimately real, its beginninglessness does not obstruct our accepted non-duality. To this [the response is]: this is a confusion — because of the impossibility of its being non-ultimate through the intermediary of a fault in a hypothesizing agent, since the <s>avidyā</s> being accepted as beginningless [cannot be dismissed so easily].

children.text: brahmaṇa eva tatkalpakadoṣatve durghaṭatvena hetvantarānapekṣatve vā muktāvapi tatprasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: If <s>Brahman</s> itself is the [agent with the] hypothesizing fault, then since [the problem is] intractable, and since no other cause is required, the same consequence would follow even in liberation.
Since an entity that is beginningless cannot undergo absolute destruction, its being removable by knowledge is also impossible — this is the gist.
Thus the impossibility of the essential nature of <s>avidyā</s> has been stated. (106)

body.text: kiñcāsau kasya ? jīvasya, ko jīvo yasya seti cet /
body.translated_text: Moreover, whose [<s>avidyā</s>] is this? If [you say] it belongs to the <s>jīva</s> (individual self) — then who is the <s>jīva</s> for whom it exists?
Indeed, in this way there would be no resolution — there would be mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>). (Verse 107)

body.text: na te jīvādavidyā syāt , na ca jīvastayā vinā /
body.translated_text: For you, <s>avidyā</s> cannot belong to the <s>jīva</s>, nor can the <s>jīva</s> exist without it.
The analogy of seed and sprout does not hold, because the origination of the <s>jīva</s> is impossible. (Verse 108)

children.translated_text: 'Moreover, whose' —

children.text:
viti /
na vidyate samādhānaṃ yasya tadasamādhānam - asamādheyam /
avidyākalpito jīvabhāvaḥ, tasmin siddha evāvidyāsiddhiriti jīvāvidyāpakṣe paramate 'nyonyāśrayo 'samādheyaḥ prasajatītyarthaḥ /
asmanmate 'kalpitatvājjīvasya tatrāvidyopagame na doṣaḥ /
kintu bhavatāmeveti dyotyate
children.translated_text: thus. That for which there is no resolution — that is unresolvable. The status of being a <s>jīva</s> is fabricated by <s>avidyā</s>, and the establishment of <s>avidyā</s> [depends on] that [<s>jīva</s>] being already established — thus, in the opponent's view, where <s>avidyā</s> belongs to the <s>jīva</s>, there is unresolvable mutual dependence. Such is the meaning. In our view, since the <s>jīva</s> is not fabricated [by <s>avidyā</s>], accepting <s>avidyā</s> in relation to it involves no fault. But for you [Advaitins] alone — this is indicated
by 'your'

children.text:
iti nirdeśena /
jīvādityasyāgre 'pi vināpadaṃ yojyam /
narteiti vā pāṭhaḥ sambhāvyate /
bījāṅkura nyāyena sa doṣaḥ parihārya ityatrāha
children.translated_text: in the reference. After 'from the <s>jīva</s>,' the word 'without' should also be connected. Or the reading 'narte' (not without) may be considered. To the objection that the fault can be resolved by the analogy of seed and sprout, he says:
'Not' —

children.text:
ti /
bījāṅkurapravāhe tvanyānyasya bījasyāṅkurasya cotpādyotpādakabhāvaḥ /
naivaṃ prakṛte sambhavati /
ekajīvasthāne 'nekajīvaprasaṅgājjīvānāmutpādavināśaprasaṅgāccetibhāvaḥ //107 //108 //
children.translated_text: thus. In the stream of seed and sprout, each successive seed and sprout has a producer-produced relationship with the other. But this is not possible in the present case. Because [if <s>avidyā</s> produces <s>jīva</s> and <s>jīva</s> produces <s>avidyā</s>], in the place of one <s>jīva</s> there would absurdly be many <s>jīvas</s>, and <s>jīvas</s> would absurdly undergo origination and destruction — such is the purport. (107)(108)

body.translated_text: Now he states the impossibility of the locus of <s>avidyā</s>:

body.text: brahmaṇaścenna sarvajñaṃ kathaṃ tat baṃbhramīti te(bhoḥ) /
body.translated_text: If [<s>avidyā</s> belongs] to <s>Brahman</s> — how can that omniscient [<s>Brahman</s>] be deluded? So say you!
The dependence [of <s>Brahman</s>'s omniscience] upon the cognition of self as body, which is produced by <s>avidyā</s>, is not [the case] for you;
[Because] the omniscient nature of <s>Brahman</s> is heard [in scripture] as its intrinsic nature. (Verse 109)

children.translated_text: 'Of <s>Brahman</s>' —

children.text:
iti /
sarvaṃ sarvadā sarvathā yathāvasthitaṃ svataḥ sākṣātkurvatastasya nānāvidhabhrāntilakṣaṇāvidyāśrayatvaṃ viruddhatvānna sambhavatītyarthaḥ /
brahma bambhramītīti te 'bhimataṃ kathaṃ ghaṭate ? tasya sarvajñatvena bhramāyogāditi bhāvaḥ /
nanu saṃvinmātraṃ brahma /
tasya sārvajñyamapyavidyākalpitaṃ mithyābhedaprapañcasadbhāvagocaraṃ bhrāntilakṣaṇaṃ mithyaivetyatrāha
children.translated_text: thus. For that [<s>Brahman</s>] which directly perceives everything, always, in every way, as it is, from its own nature — being the locus of <s>avidyā</s>, characterized by various forms of delusion, is impossible because of contradiction. Such is the meaning. '<s>Brahman</s> is deluded' — how does this view of yours hold up? Because delusion is impossible for an omniscient being — such is the purport. Objection: <s>Brahman</s> is mere consciousness; its omniscience too is fabricated by <s>avidyā</s>, having as its object the existent world of false differentiation, and being characterized by delusion, is itself false. To this he says:
'Produced by <s>avidyā</s>' —

children.text:
ti /
te ityasyāgre 'bhimateti śeṣaḥ /
avidyāmūlāhaṅkāranibandhanatā ca brahmaniṣṭhasya sārvajñyasya na ghaṭate,
children.translated_text: thus. After 'your,' 'accepted' is to be supplied. And the dependence [of omniscience] on the ego-sense rooted in <s>avidyā</s> does not hold for <s>Brahman</s>'s omniscience,

children.text: parāsya śaktirvividhaiva śrūyate svābhāvikī jñānabalakriyā ceti
children.translated_text: 'His supreme power is heard of as manifold, innate — the power of knowledge, strength, and action' —
because there is the scriptural testimony that it [<s>Brahman</s>'s knowledge] is not dependent on any other qualification. Such is the meaning.
The interpretation that <s>avidyā</s> is the nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>, and that [omniscience is called] 'innate' because it is rooted in that [<s>avidyā</s>] — this is laughable.
And since one's nature cannot be overcome, if that were so, <s>Brahman</s> would always be ignorant and there would absurdly be no liberation — this should be understood. (109)

body.translated_text: Objection: then let <s>Brahman</s> itself be the locus of <s>avidyā</s>. To this he says:
If omniscience is false because it contains the appearance of difference,
Then for the very same reason, why should it not be true — just as in the case of another word [i.e., scriptural authority] and the like? (Verse 110)

children.translated_text: 'Difference' —
thus. The word 'if' (<s>atha</s>) has the sense of 'suppose.' 'For the very same reason' — precisely because it contains the appearance of difference.
'Not false' — having a veridical object.
Through the first and second halves [of the verse], the opponent's position and the established conclusion are respectively presented.
The very falsity of difference is unestablished;
therefore that whose appearance contains [difference] would [also not be false] — such is the import. (110)

body.translated_text: Having thus refuted [omniscience's] being fabricated by <s>avidyā</s>, he also refutes [the claim] that omniscience is not veridical because it contains the appearance of difference:
Just as another word [of scripture], repetition, number, and so forth are determiners of [ritual] distinction,
And contain the appearance of difference, yet are veridical — why should [omniscience] not be likewise? (Verse 111)

children.translated_text: 'Just as another word' —
he elaborates on what was stated:
'Just as' —
thus.
In the <s>Pūrvamīmāṃsā</s>, distinction of [ritual] action is determined through another word [of scripture], repetition, number, name, quality, and a different context.

children.text: te śabdāntarādayaḥ śāstrabhedakāḥ-tattadvidhivākyasya vibhinnavibhinnavidheyakatvena bhedavyavasthāpakāḥ bhedakapramāṇabhūtāstāntrikairmatāḥ, tanmūlā vidheyabhedapratyayāśca yathārthā eva yathā ; tathā sarvajñatāpi pāramārthikārthabhedagocarā yathārthaiva kiṃ na syādityarthaḥ // 111 //
children.translated_text: Those [determiners] — another word and the rest — are determiners of [ritual] distinction in the <s>śāstra</s>, that is, they are the authoritative means of establishing difference by making each injunctive sentence have a different thing to be enjoined. And the cognitions of distinction arising from them are accepted by the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> as veridical; just as [those cognitions of difference are veridical], so too why should omniscience not be veridical with reference to real, ultimate differentiation of objects? Such is the meaning. (111)

body.translated_text: If in the omniscient and eternally liberated [<s>Brahman</s>] there were the possibility of ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>),
Like darkness in fire, it would then never be removed by anything. (Verse 112)

body.text:
parabrahmaṇi parameśvare svataḥ sarvajñe 'vidyāyā asambhava uktaḥ /
tatra tadupagame bādhakaṃ cāha

children.translated_text: 'Omniscient' —

children.text:
iti /
nityamuktasvabhāvatvātsarvajñatvācca bandhakāvidyāpratibhaṭe sarveśvara eva yadyavidyā vindeta padaṃ gabhastimālinīvāndhatamasaṃ tarhi na tasyā nivartakamanyatkiñcidapi sambhavedityanivṛttiprasaṅga ityarthaḥ /
nanu tattvamasītivākyajanyāparokṣacinmātrabrahmātmaikyasākṣātkāreṇaivāvidyānivṛttiriti cet , naitatsādhu, vākyasyāparokṣajanakatvābhāvāt , śukādeḥ sākṣātkāreṇaivāvidyānivṛtteḥ saṃsāropalambhavirodhāt , ekajīvavādasya ca nirākariṣyamāṇatvāt /
kiñca brahma svāvidyayā bambhramīti, jīvaḥ svavidyayā tadunmocayatīti viparītamidamadhyātmadarśanaṃ vedāntivikhyātānām /
svarūpavyākriyaivaitanmatasya parākriyā /
tathā cāmananti sma parāśarabhaṭṭapādāḥ
children.translated_text: thus. Since [<s>Brahman</s>] is of an eternally liberated nature and is omniscient — the very opponent of binding <s>avidyā</s> — if <s>avidyā</s> were to find a foothold in the all-sovereign one, like darkness in the sun, then no other remover of it could possibly exist — there would be the absurd consequence of its being unremovable. Such is the meaning. Objection: <s>avidyā</s> is removed precisely by the immediate realization of the identity of the self with <s>Brahman</s> — which is mere consciousness — produced by the sentence '<s>tattvamasi</s>.' Response: This is not correct, because the sentence [alone] cannot generate immediate perception; because if <s>avidyā</s> is removed by [<s>Brahman</s>'s] direct realization itself — as in the case of a parrot and the like — then the perception of <s>saṃsāra</s> would be contradicted; and because the single-<s>jīva</s> doctrine will be refuted [later]. Moreover, '<s>Brahman</s> is deluded by its own ignorance, and the <s>jīva</s> liberates it by his own knowledge' — this is the topsy-turvy spiritual doctrine of the well-known Vedāntins! The very exposition of this doctrine is itself its refutation. And thus the revered <s>Parāśara Bhaṭṭa</s> declared:

children.text: etadrāmāstraṃ dalayatu kalibrahmamīmāṃsakāṃśca jñaptirbrahmaitajjavaladapi nijāvidyayā bambhramīti /
children.translated_text: 'May this arrow of <s>Rāma</s> shatter those <s>Brahma</s>-<s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> of the Kali [age] who made known [the doctrine that] consciousness is <s>Brahman</s>, and that even this [<s>Brahman</s>], though luminous, is deluded by its own ignorance;

children.text: tasya bhrāntiṃ tāṃ ślathayati jitādvaitavidyastu jīvo yadyaddṛśyaṃ tadvitathamiti ye jñāpayāñcakrurajñāḥ //
children.translated_text: And who, [as] the <s>jīva</s> that has conquered that Advaita-knowledge, loosens that delusion of it [<s>Brahman</s>] — and who have demonstrated that whatever is perceived is false — [they are] the ignorant ones!'

body.translated_text: It has been stated that <s>avidyā</s> is impossible in the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Lord, who is inherently omniscient. He also states the absurd consequence if it is accepted:
'We do not see any determinant — that the Advaita-statements [of scripture] are authoritative —
other than your mere insistence.' (Verse 113)

body.text:
nanu bhedakapramāṇānāṃ sarvajñatvādivacanānāmapi vyāvahārikārthabhedagocarāṇāṃ vyāvahārikameva pramāṇyam /
paramārthapramāṇatvaṃ tvadvaitavacasāmeva /
paramārthastu paraṃ brahma nirviśeṣasaccinmātrameva /
tatra jīveśvarādibhedo 'pyavidyayā vinānupapanna iti brahmāśritaiva sānāyatyā mantavyeti śaṅkate

children.translated_text: 'Omniscience and the like' —
thus. He refutes this:
'Determinant' —

children.text:
iti /
tvatkalpitasaṅketabalena vinā naivaṃvidhavyavasthāyāṃ kiñcana pramāṇamasti /
children.translated_text: thus. Without the force of a conventional designation fabricated by you, there is absolutely no authority for such a system.
And scripture is not authoritative for the meaning you state.
For thus: since the dual and non-dual <s>śrutis</s> [respectively] teach the plurality of modes and the oneness of what has those modes, neither is false in its purport.

children.text: sāmānādhikaraṇyaśrutīnāṃ ca sarvaśarīrakasarvātmabhūtabrahmaikyaparatvamiti na jīvabhāvādikalpikāvidyā brahmaṇyupagantavyeti ca hārdam /
children.translated_text: And the co-referential <s>śrutis</s> teach the oneness with <s>Brahman</s> that is the inner self of all bodies and the self of all — therefore <s>avidyā</s> fabricating the status of <s>jīva</s> and the like need not be accepted as having its locus in <s>Brahman</s>. This is the gist.
And this has been elaborated at the very beginning [of the work] — so we stop here. (113)

body.translated_text: Objection: The authoritative means that establish difference — such as statements about omniscience and the like — also have only conventional (<s>vyāvahārika</s>) authority, since they deal with conventional differentiation of objects. But ultimate authority belongs only to the Advaita-statements. The ultimate reality is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> — mere undifferentiated existence-consciousness alone. The difference of <s>jīva</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, and the like therein is also impossible without <s>avidyā</s>. Therefore <s>avidyā</s> must definitely be accepted as having its locus in <s>Brahman</s> — thus the objection:

children.translated_text: Being the locus [of <s>avidyā</s>] and being the counterpositive [of <s>avidyā</s>] are mutually contradictory.
How does one cognize <s>Brahman</s> as of one taste (<s>ekarasa</s>), as 'existent' (<s>sat</s>)? (Verse 114)

body.translated_text: If <s>Brahman</s> is the locus qua the inner self (<s>pratyaktva</s>), and the counterpositive qua <s>Brahman</s>-nature —
Whence does this difference of form arise? If it arises by the grace of <s>avidyā</s>,
Then since that [<s>avidyā</s>] too depends on that [distinction] — once again there is mutual dependence. (Verse 115)

children.translated_text: 'Being the locus' —

thus. 'Being the counterpositive' here has the sense of being the object. The contradiction intended is that of being simultaneously the agent and the object [of the same action] in one and the same [entity].
'Mutually contradictory' —

children.text:
ti /
saditi sattāmātramekarasaṃ svaprakāśarūpaṃ brahma kathaṃ svaviṣayakāvidyāyatanaṃ bhavedākārabhedābhāvāditi bhāvaḥ /
ākārabhedenāvirodhamāśaṅkate
children.translated_text: thus. How can <s>Brahman</s> — which is of one taste (<s>ekarasa</s>), of the nature of self-luminosity, [cognized] merely as 'existent' (<s>sat</s>) — be the substratum of <s>avidyā</s> whose object is itself, given the absence of any differentiation of form? Such is the purport. Anticipating the objection that there is no contradiction through a difference of form:
'Qua the inner self' —

children.text:
ti /
sanmātrameva brahma svaprakāśatvarūpeṇāhantvarūpeṇa vā pratyaktvenāśrayo 'vidyāyāḥ, brahmatvena viṣaya iti cedayaṃ rūpabhedaḥ kathamāyātastatra ? yadyavidyayā, anyonyāśrayaprasaṅgaḥ /
svābhāviko 'yamiti tu na vaktuṃ śakyate saviśeṣatvabhiyā parairiti bhāvaḥ jīvāvidyāpakṣa ivātrāpyanyonyāśra iti punarityanena dyotyate // 114 //115 //
children.translated_text: thus. If <s>Brahman</s>, being mere existence (<s>sanmātra</s>), is the locus of <s>avidyā</s> qua its self-luminous form or qua its 'I'-form (<s>ahantvam</s>) — that is, qua its inner-self aspect — and is the object [of <s>avidyā</s>] qua its <s>Brahman</s>-nature, then whence does this difference of form arise? If through <s>avidyā</s>, then there is the consequence of mutual dependence. And the opponents cannot say 'this [difference] is innate,' out of their fear of [admitting] qualification [in <s>Brahman</s>] — such is the purport. That here too, as in the position where <s>avidyā</s> belongs to the <s>jīva</s>, there is mutual dependence — this is indicated by the word 'again' (<s>punar</s>). (114)(115)

body.translated_text: He states another objection to <s>Brahman</s> being the locus of <s>avidyā</s>:

children.text:
diti /
aparamārthāvidyāyā durghaṭatvaṃ bhūṣaṇameva /
nāto 'nyānyāśrayaṇaṃ doṣarūpamiti pūrvordhena śaṅkānuvādaḥ /
pariharati

body.text: kiñcāvidyā na cet ... (vastu vyavahāryaṃ kathaṃ bhavet ) /
nāpyavastviti co....... (ktau tu vastutvaṃ sidhyati dhruvam ) /
ato na vastu nā... (vastu na sadvācyaṃ na cāpyasat ) /

children.text:
ti /
atra katipaye ślokāvaluptabhūyoṃ'śakā upalabhyante 'śuddhibahulāśca /
dṛśyamānaśakalānusandhānataḥ avidyāyā na vastutvaṃ nāpyavastutvamiti pakṣasya pratikṣepaḥ kṛto 'tretyunnayāmaḥ /

body.translated_text: Moreover, those who know practical affairs [say that] when, despite the presence of a complete cause,

body.text: kāryaṃ na jāyate yena tamāhuḥ pratibandhakam // 142 //
body.translated_text: an effect does not arise, they call that [which prevents it] an obstructor (<s>pratibandhaka</s>). // 142 //
Here, what is it that, having begun to arise from its own cause,
does not attain arising because it is obstructed by <s>avidyā</s>? // 143 //
Not liberation, because it is eternally accomplished. Nor the cognition 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' either.
For the cognition 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' is not the complete cause [of liberation].
If the transmigrating being possesses it, how is it obstructed? // 144 //
Since that [cognition] does not arise at present because of the absence of its cause,
and not because it is obstructed—therefore, the statement of that [obstructing function of <s>avidyā</s>] is misplaced. // 145 //

children.translated_text: (Thus, the examination of the purposelessness of effort toward liberation in the single-<s>jīva</s> theory.)
Now he says that the opponent's statement that <s>avidyā</s> is an obstructor of the manifestation of the eternally liberated nature is also untenable:
'Moreover'—

children.translated_text: thus. Obstructing means preventing the arising of an effect when the complete cause is present. Since liberation is not something to be produced, the obstructing function of <s>avidyā</s> with respect to it does not work. And for the transmigrating being, in the state of being inclined toward sense objects, since there is simply the non-attainment of the complete causal conditions for direct realization of reality, its non-arising [is due to that]—so there too the obstructing function of <s>avidyā</s> does not apply. This is the meaning. '<s>saṃvidaḥ puṣkalakāraṇam</s>' is a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound [meaning 'the complete cause of cognition']. In the established doctrine [of <s>Viśiṣṭādvaita</s>], however, <s>avidyā</s>, which is of the nature of the prior absence of knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), does not obstruct knowledge. Rather, it is <s>karma</s>—which is the cause of the non-arising of knowledge—[that must be dealt with]: when it is removed by desireless actions (<s>niṣkāmakarma</s>), knowledge arises from its own cause. And through the greatness of knowledge, when binding <s>karma</s> ceases, the <s>dharmabhūtajñāna</s> (attributive knowledge), whose expansion had been contracted by <s>karma</s>, attains its natural uncontracted expansion, which is [the state of being] ever liberated. This distinction should be understood. Here the opponents would counter: 'In our view too, <s>avidyā</s> is accepted as beginningless, causing unclear manifestation and being the cause of manifold delusion. Upon its removal by knowledge, there is the natural clear manifestation. And precisely because it obstructs clear manifestation, the designation of it as an obstructor is appropriate.' To them we say: Does this 'obstructing of clear manifestation' mean obstructing its arising, or causing its removal? If clear manifestation is different from the essential nature of <s>Brahman</s>, then <s>Brahman</s> would have qualifications, entailing the consequence that <s>Brahman</s> is qualified (<s>saviśeṣa</s>). If it is to be said to be non-different [from <s>Brahman</s>'s nature], then since it is not something to be produced, the obstructing of its [arising] is not possible—so the first alternative fails. In the second alternative, there would be the consequence of the cessation of the very nature of <s>Brahman</s>. Nor can it be said by the proponent of qualityless [<s>Brahman</s>] that only the clarity ceases while the luminosity continues. Furthermore, when <s>avidyā</s>, which obstructs clear manifestation, exists, how can direct realization occur? If that [realization] too is unclear, then, like the initial knowledge from hearing, it would not be capable of removing <s>avidyā</s>. Furthermore, upon the removal of <s>avidyā</s> there is clear direct realization, and by that very [clear realization] <s>avidyā</s> is removed—[this is] mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>). Furthermore, if the clear experience that occurs immediately after the removal of <s>avidyā</s> did not exist previously, liberation would be non-eternal; if it did exist [previously], <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) would be impossible—[both] unwanted consequences follow. Nor should it be said that freedom from <s>avidyā</s> is itself the clarity of self-luminosity—for since in the self-luminous nature alone, the ever-shining, qualityless, mere consciousness that is <s>Brahman</s>, there can be no connection of <s>avidyā</s>, clarity itself must be accepted as existing even prior [to liberation]. And if it is said that <s>avidyā</s> somehow operates there despite the difficulty—then for the very same reason, in liberation too the connection of <s>avidyā</s> would follow, and even the liberated one would have cause for fear. // 142 // 143 // 144 // 145 //

body.translated_text: Moreover, [the assertion that] there is a single <s>jīva</s>—this is not consistent with the actual state of things.
<s>Avidyā</s>, its connection with that [consciousness], <s>jīva</s>-hood, and the like are false (<s>mṛṣā</s>) for you. // 146 //

Either one <s>jīva</s> or [many]—neither is ultimately accepted [by the <s>Advaitin</s>].
Because <s>jīva</s>-hood is false, being fabricated by false <s>avidyā</s>.

children.text: tathā ca mithyābhūtasyaikasyānekasya vā jīvasyopagame na viśeṣo vinābhiniveśādityarthaḥ // 146 //
children.translated_text: And thus, whether one accepts a single or multiple false <s>jīvas</s>, there is no difference—except out of [mere] insistence. This is the meaning. // 146 //

body.translated_text: The refutations against the single-<s>jīva</s> theory have been stated. Now he states that it is also contradicted by experience:
The phenomenal oneness is contradicted by phenomenal appearance,
since thousands of transmigrating beings appear to us. // 147 //

body.text: eko jīva iti kimekasyaiva pratibhāsādupagamyate, āhosvinnānātvena bhāsamānasyāpi tasya yuktyaikatvaṃ niṣkṛṣyata iti vikalpamabhipretyādyaṃ kalpaṃ dūṣayati

body.translated_text: Is the single <s>jīva</s> accepted because only one appears, or is its oneness extracted by reasoning even though it appears as many? With the intention of [examining] this alternative, he first refutes the first option:
Until the complete cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the practical transactions caused by that [plurality of <s>jīvas</s>]
are perceived as unrefuted, and unlike the behavior [experienced] in dreams. // 148 //
